description: Intent i031 (SNAPSHOT=s08, BRANCH=unclamped-wire-count) complete. Finding 1 (medium confidence): s08:net/bluetooth/hci_event.c:7254-7279, hci_store_wake_reason() LE meta branch — untrusted source is the controller/virtual-HCI-transport event payload; the wire count is fetched raw at line 7258 'u8 num_reports = *ptr;' with no hci_ev_skb_pull, no skb->len check, and no min_len check, and its non-zero value gates immediate dereference of adv/direct_adv/ext_adv = (void *)(ptr + 1) (lines 7264-7266) whose fields are copied into persistent kernel state hdev->wake_addr/wake_addr_type (bacpy at 7270/7274/7278) — OOB read into hdev state. Asymmetric validation verified: sibling handlers of the same event family all validate the count against the received length (hci_le_adv_report_evt:6225 per-report hci_le_ev_skb_pull(sizeof(*info)) and (info->length+1); hci_le_ext_adv_report_evt:6309 same; hci_le_direct_adv_report_evt:6645 flex_array_size pull; hci_le_meta_evt:7169 skb->len < subev->min_len; hci_event_func:7468 hci_ev_skb_pull), and the entry path hci_event_packet:7489 checks only skb->len >= sizeof(*hdr) (2 bytes) before skb_pull(HCI_EVENT_HDR_SIZE) at 7531 and the call at 7534, so truncated LE meta events reach the *ptr fetch. Reachability bounded by the suspended-first-event gate (line 7236). Seed usbip family confirmed present UNPATCHED in s08 (usbip_common.c:473 verbatim 'urb->number_of_packets = rpdu->number_of_packets;' store, :664-665 'int np = urb->number_of_packets; int size = np * sizeof(*iso);', USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS enforced only on the CMD_SUBMIT sibling at stub_rx.c:379-381) and recorded as an excluded-by-rule unresolved candidate per the seed-never-reportable rule. Limitations: the finalize directive stopped the planned broad sweep of other s08 deserialization entry points (netlink nla handlers, fs/ceph, fs/cifs, ksmbd, 9p, nbd, io_uring, HID/NCI) at enumeration level; impact is a bounded OOB read into persistent state with userspace exposure untraced; no runtime reproducer was built (read-only tree).
